stem: A client is on Contact Precautions. Which PPE is required for interactions that may involve contact with the client or environment?

options.A: Wear a surgical mask and perform hand hygiene; a gown and gloves are unnecessary.
options.B: Wear eye protection and perform hand hygiene; a gown and gloves are unnecessary.
options.C: Wear a gown and gloves for contact with the client or the client's environment.
options.D: Use hand hygiene alone because Contact Precautions do not add PPE to Standard Precautions.

rationale: CDC Transmission-Based Precautions guidance states that Contact Precautions are used in addition to Standard Precautions and directs healthcare personnel to wear a gown and gloves for all interactions that may involve contact with the patient or the patient's environment. Therefore C is correct. A, B, and D omit the core Contact Precautions barriers. Additional mask or eye protection may still be indicated under Standard Precautions for a specific anticipated splash or spray exposure, but those items do not replace gown and gloves for the contact interaction described.
educational_objective: For Contact Precautions, wear both gown and gloves when interaction may involve contact with the client or potentially contaminated environmental surfaces, while adding task-specific Standard Precautions PPE when indicated.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_locator: Recommendation details > Use Contact Precautions: Transmission-Based Precautions are used in addition to Standard Precautions; use PPE appropriately, including gloves and gown; wear a gown and gloves for all interactions that may involve contact with the patient or the patient's environment. Guideline for Isolation Precautions > Contact Precautions similarly directs gown and gloves for such interactions.
source_claim_supported: Contact Precautions require gown and gloves for interactions that may involve patient or environmental contact, in addition to Standard Precautions and any task-specific PPE indicated by exposure risk.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — apply Standard and Transmission-Based Precautions and select/use PPE to prevent transmission of infection.
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Contact Precautions PPE

source_original.rationale: CDC Contact Precautions call for gown and gloves for interactions involving the patient or patient environment. Additional PPE may be required under Standard Precautions for specific tasks. Option C is correct; the other choices omit the core contact barriers.
source_original.source_detail: Contact Precautions: use gown and gloves for interactions that may involve contact with the patient or the patient's environment, in addition to Standard Precautions and task-specific PPE. CDC Transmission-Based Precautions page current; live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: transmission precautions, PPE, device/environmental safety, asepsis, identification and infection-prevention activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the original stem, options, and key C. Strengthened the rationale to explicitly preserve the distinction between the gown-and-glove requirement of Contact Precautions and additional task-specific PPE that may be indicated under Standard Precautions.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current CDC Transmission-Based Precautions guidance; NCSBN 2026 for blueprint
audit_findings.exact_locator: Transmission-Based Precautions > Use Contact Precautions; corroborated by Guideline for Isolation Precautions > Contact Precautions
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item precisely tests the CDC gown-and-glove requirement for contact interactions and does not imply that masks/eye protection are never needed; task-specific Standard Precautions remain applicable.

distractor_audit.A: Mask/hand hygiene do not replace gown and gloves for Contact Precautions interactions.
distractor_audit.B: Eye protection/hand hygiene do not replace gown and gloves for Contact Precautions interactions.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because Contact Precautions add transmission-based PPE beyond Standard Precautions.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C includes both required Contact Precautions barriers for the interaction described.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives are PPE/hand-hygiene strategies for the same interaction; no unrelated mechanism is introduced.
audit_findings.blueprint: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — transmission precautions and PPE.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current CDC guidance, each option, Standard-versus-Contact distinction, rationale, objective, NCSBN mapping, ambiguity and cueing. C remained uniquely correct.
